t_series.note: The T-series (fabric strips with dim blue flames) cannot be followed by the tracker. These outcomes were graded by SI from brightened frames and the fan voltage history, blind to NASA's outcomes, and compared afterwards with NASA's Table 7.1.
t_series.graded_by: SI (Claude Sonnet) viewing brightened frames, blind to NASA's outcomes, 2026-11-14
t_series.check_note: One team member checked the SI grades against video brightened x6, without looking at NASA's outcomes (they were hidden on the review page; the checker states this, the check was not supervised).

tests.label: T4
tests.reason: A bright ignition flash at 4-5 s is followed by a dim two-lobed crescent flame beside the wire. It faded as the fan was stepped down from 80 and was gone by about 13 s at FAN about 56. Weak flame and short life, so medium.
tests.fan_history: 80 at ignition (to 7 s); 73 at 8 s; 67 at 10 s; 59 at 12 s; 54 at 16 s; 46 from 26 s

checked.note: flame seems to be still very slightly visible after 13 s

tests.label: T9
tests.reason: Only a thin horizontal red wire glow with a faint reddish haze above it; no blue or separate flame at any time; fan never changed.

checked.note: after initial ignition there seem to be a very small flame, very possible for it to be the wire

tests.label: T10
tests.reason: A large bright red glow burned 16-23 s and vanished within about 1 s with the fan unchanged; nothing was visible after 24 s, and when the fan was raised at 80 s nothing was burning. Could be a short-lived flame that died by itself; low confidence.
tests.fan_history: 47-48 until about 78 s; 73 at 80 s; 105 at 82 s; 122 at 84 s

tests.label: T12
tests.reason: A bright white-red glow starts at 12 s and is still there when the video ends at 45 s, with no fan change. I cannot separate wire glow from a flame, and no fan action is shown to tell the outcome.

checked.note: multiple attempts at ignition most likely

tests.label: T13
tests.reason: After the wire flash a faint two-lobed flame sits at the wire from 32 s and fades by about 50 s while the fan eased from 46 to 42. It was already fading at constant fan, so the cause is uncertain. The later rise to 122 came with nothing burning. Low.
tests.fan_history: 46 at ignition and to about 40 s; 44 at 46 s; 42 from 52 s to about 95 s; 47 at 100 s; 122 at 110 s (read by eye)

tests.label: T14
tests.reason: A very faint blue-green flame stays at the wire from 34 s to about 115 s while the fan creeps down 47 to 43 and RAD rises; it fades out and RAD collapses after 112 s. Fan changes are small and the flame is very faint, so medium.

checked.note: way too hard to spot towards the end

tests.label: T15
tests.reason: A clear two-lobed flame lights as the fan is raised to 122, grows and travels along the strip for about 28 s, then shrinks and leaves the picture at about 38 s. It was not blown off.
tests.fan_history: 80 at ignition; 98 at 8 s; 122 at 10 s; 122-127 to end

tests.label: T17
tests.reason: A faint flame is present at fan 42 (48-54 s); when the fan is raised to 122 it brightens and travels left for about 12 s, then shrinks and is gone at about 70 s at the left of the picture. It lasted well past the rise and ended in the same way as the surviving flame in T15, so no blow-off; medium because the end could be a late blow-off.
tests.fan_history: 42 until about 55 s; 62 at 56 s; 88 at 58 s; 112 at 60 s; 122 from 62 s

tests.label: T18
tests.reason: A very faint flame burned at the wire from 30 s to about 68 s while the fan was stepped down 46 to 41 (AIR falling to 0); it faded out at low flow. The later fan rise came with nothing burning.
tests.fan_history: 46-47 to about 48 s; 45 at 50 s; 42 at 54 s; 41 from 58 s; 53 at 80 s; 96 at 82 s (after the flame was gone)

tests.label: T20
tests.reason: no plain main video on PSI

tests.label: T21
tests.reason: A faint flame (24-31 s) brightens as the fan is raised and travels left, then disappears between 34 and 35 s just as the fan reaches 122, with nothing after.

checked.note: flame can be clearly seen while ignition glow is still visible

tests.label: T22
tests.reason: A faint blue flame (20-41 s) burns on while the fan is stepped down 67 to 52 and fades out at about 42 s at low flow.
